s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Progressive skin lesions for more than 10 years
Lesions localized to the left shin
Itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Histopathologic examination revealed several milia in the superficial dermis
Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1

shortlist.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, which is a known cause of this condition

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation and milia, consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoepidermal separation and milia are also features of this condition, although the genetic findings are more suggestive of Dystrophic EB

shortlist.label: Kindler Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: This condition also involves skin fragility and blistering, and can present with similar histopathologic findings

shortlist.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: While less likely given the genetic findings, this condition can also present with blistering skin lesions and dermoepidermal separation

raw.rationale: The presence of progressive skin lesions with milia, erosions, and dermoepidermal separation, along with a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, is consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
rejected.why: Lack of familial history and specific genetic mutations typical of EBS

rejected.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: Absence of mucous membrane involvement and specific histopathological findings

rejected.label: Kindler Syndrome
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and genetic findings do not align with Kindler Syndrome

rejected.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
rejected.why: Age of onset, clinical presentation, and genetic findings are not consistent with Bullous Pemphigoid
